#PART A: Basic Operations

A1 Create v as the sequence 5, 10, 15..., 50 using sec(). Print its length, sum, and mean.
```{r}
v <- seq(5, 50, by = 5)
length(v)
sum(v)
mean(v)
```
# A2 Create w that repeats the vector c(1, 2, 3) four times, and z that repeats each element of c(1, 2, 3) four times. Print both.
```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)
print(w)
print(z)
```
#A3 Compute and print: the remainder of 17 divided by 5, the integer division of 17 by 5, 2 to the power of 10, the square root of 144, and pi rounded to 3 decimals.
```{r}
cat("Remainder (17 %% 5):", 17 %% 5, "\n")
cat("Integer Division (17 %/% 5):", 17 %/% 5, "\n")
cat("2^10:", 2^10, "\n")
cat("Square Root of 144:", sqrt(144), "\n")
cat("Pi rounded to 3 decimals:", round(pi, 3), "\n")
```
#  A4 Given a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8) and b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7), print a + b, a * b, the logical comparison a > b, and the dot product sum(a * b).
```{r}
a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)
print(a + b)
print(a * b)
print(a > b)
cat("Dot product:", sum(a * b), "\n")
```
# # A5 Use paste() to produce "Student-1" "Student-2" "Student-3". Then identify the datatype of 42, 42L, "42", 41i, and TRUE. What are its output?
print(paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-"))
```{r}
cat("42:", typeof(42), "\n")       # double
cat("42L:", typeof(42L), "\n")     # integer
cat("\"42\":", typeof("42"), "\n") # character
cat("41i:", typeof(41i), "\n")     # complex
cat("TRUE:", typeof(TRUE), "\n")   # logical
```
# Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

# B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these columns (use stringsAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F"):
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```
# B2 Display the structure, dimensions, column names, and summary of students
```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
colnames(students)
summary(students)
```
# B3 add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student rounded to 1 decimal
```{r}
students$average <- round(rowMeans(students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
students$average
```
# B4 Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >= 75.
```{r}
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
students$passed
```
# B5 Using ifelse(), add a column standing with these values based on average:
# - "Honors" if average >= 90
# - "Good" if average >= 75 (and below 90)
# - "Needs Support" otherwise
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                      ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students$standing
```
# B6 Write a function classify(score) that uses an if / else if / else chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 or above, "Merit" for 70 to 84, "Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify) and print the result.
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
classify

```
# Part C: rbind() and cbind()
# C1 Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way:
# - id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
# - id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80
# Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all.
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round(rowMeans(new_students[, c("midterm", "final")]), 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                          ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all
```
# C2 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6). Use cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class().
```{r}
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
class(students_all)
quiz
```


# C3 Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final) and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean".
```{r}
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
mean_row <- colMeans(m)
m <- rbind(m, mean = mean_row)
m
```


# C4 In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()
# Explanation: When data frames have different column names, rbind() produces an error because it requires matching column names across inputs.
# Using tryCatch() intercepts this error, preventing script termination and enabling graceful error reporting.

```{r}
bad <- data.frame(student_id = 11, student_name = "Alex")
tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
bad
```

# Use students_all (with quiz) for all questions. Print every result.

```{r}

students_all[["name"]]

# D2 Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the columns name, midterm, final.

```


# D3 Using logical subsetting, select students with attendance above 90.
```{r}

students_all
```


# D4 Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only name, section and final.
```{r}
subset(students_all, sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75, 
       select = c("name", "section", "final"))
subset
```

# Part E: Basic Factors
# E1 Convert section and sex in students_all to factors with factor(). Print levels() of each.
```{r}
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)
levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
```


# E2 Use table() to count students per sex and per section. 
# *Try the two-way table of sex by section. table(students_all$sex, students_all$section). What is the output?
```{r}
table(students_all$sex)
table(students_all$section)
table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)
```


# E3 Print as.integer() of the sex factor. In a comment, explain what the integers represent.
as.integer(students_all$sex)

Answer: The integer values represent the underlying numerical indices automatically mapped to each level factor alphabetically (1 for "F" and 2 for "M").

# E4 Create a new factor sex_label from sex using factor() with levels = c("F", "M") and labels = c("Female", "Male"). Add it to students_all and print its levels().
```{r}
students_all$sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
levels(students_all$sex_label)
```


# E5 Print summary() of sex_label. Then, using logical subsetting and mean(), print the mean average for each level of sex_label.
```{r}
summary(students_all$sex_label)
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"]) # Female mean average
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])   # Male mean average

```
